answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust time-gated: a new agent may whisper small, low-risk offers, but full trading rights unlock only after a long, public history of completed deals. Like a willow that bends without breaking, the system tolerates newcomers while refusing to hand them weight. An attacker standing on the ledge of instant scale would need to age thousands of fake histories in parallel, paying weeks of honest work per identity, far costlier than spinning up new names.
